title: GVARP: Detecting Performance Variance on Large-Scale Heterogeneous Systems
problem: Performance variance in large-scale heterogeneous systems arising from random hardware and software faults causes unpredictable performance degradation in parallel programs. Pinpointing the exact causes of performance variance in specific instances is exceedingly difficult.
motivation: Performance variance leads to unexpected and unpredictable performance degradation that degrades the reliability and predictability of parallel applications on large-scale systems.
method: GVARP examines code (without running it) to find which inputs and settings most affect speed in kernel functions. It breaks program execution into segments at points where external libraries are called or asynchronous operations occur (operations that don't wait for completion). For each segment, it builds a graph tracking how data flows and measures how much computation happens. By grouping segments with similar workloads, it detects when identical code unexpectedly runs at different speeds.
key_novelty: It tracks data flow through a program and groups segments by workload to detect when identical code runs at different speeds in large-scale heterogeneous systems.
contributions: GVARP tool for detecting performance variance at large scale with acceptable overhead
Static analysis methodology for identifying performance-critical kernel parameters
State transfer graph and workload estimation approach for variance detection
Techniques for intuitive insights into sources of performance variance
primary_theme: Performance variance detection and diagnosis in heterogeneous HPC systems
